user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** To demonstrate meaningful improvement in patient-reported bone pain, physical functioning, and fatigue versus standard of care while avoiding tolerance-limiting side effects in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients.

**Key challenge:** No validated bone pain instrument was identified for the core FDA domains — EORTC QLQ-MY20 captures myeloma-specific bone pain within its Disease Symptoms subscale but lacks standalone regulatory precedent.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + MY20 combination (demonstrated change detection in [TI-003], [TI-004], [TI-005]), BFI for fatigue (score 68 with change evidence), and EQ-5D-5L for HTA requirements.

**Critical gap:** Disease-related bone pain domain lacks a dedicated validated instrument — QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale includes bone pain items  but is embedded within broader symptom assessment .

## Table 3: Instrument Gap Analysis

| Instrument | Content Validity | MCID Evidence | Regulatory Acceptance | Known Gaps / Risks | Fit for Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 |  Validated in oncology with acceptable reliability coefficients  | 10 points for functioning/symptom scales, anchor-based, MM population |  FDA/EMA accepted in MM trials; used in multiple approved MM drugs but rarely resulted in label claims  | Generally supportive evidence only — lacks primary endpoint precedent | Likely fit |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 |  Validated MM-specific module with adequate psychometric properties  | 10 points for multi-item scales, distribution-based estimate |  FDA/EMA accepted when used with QLQ-C30; provides MM-specific context but not standalone evidence  | No standalone label claims documented — requires QLQ-C30 combination | Likely fit |
| BFI |  Accepted by FDA and EMA as validated fatigue PRO instrument for secondary endpoints  | 1.33 points total scale, anchor-based, brain/CNS cancer population |  FDA 2024 Core PRO guidance is instrument-agnostic; BFI meets structural criteria but has fewer label precedents than FACIT-Fatigue  | MCID established in different cancer population — may require MM-specific validation | Conditionally fit — verify MM population MCID |
| EQ-5D-5L |  Currently preferred EuroQol instrument for FDA/EMA oncology submissions  | 0.037-0.044 index score, England 5L value set |  NICE England accepts EQ-5D-5L with England value set as primary utility evidence; FDA Core PRO Guidance recognises utility measures  | Country-specific value sets required — not universally mappable to 3L | Likely fit |
| PRO-CTCAE | Validated for symptomatic adverse event assessment in oncology | Not established via anchor methods — typically reported as mean score | Not cited by FDA/EMA as accepted oncology PRO for drug labelling claims | FDA Core PRO guidance does not specify PRO-CTCAE as preferred AE instrument | Conditionally fit — regulatory precedent unclear |

## Key Observations

•  Three of five KG PI trials demonstrated significant PRO improvements , with TOURMALINE-MM3 showing p<0.05 for both QLQ-C30 and QLQ-MY20 endpoints (Table 2, TOURMALINE-MM3 row). This supports sensitivity to detect PI treatment benefits versus standard care. •  EORTC QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale includes bone pain items (bone aches, back pain, hip pain, arm/shoulder pain, chest pain) , directly addressing the bone pain TPP claim (Table 1, disease-related bone pain row). However, this is embedded within a broader symptom construct rather than standalone pain assessment. •  Recent MM regulatory rejections cite hierarchical testing failure, missing multiplicity adjustment, and lack of pre-specification  as primary rejection reasons. Table 4 positioning must ensure PRO endpoints fall within the confirmatory alpha-controlled testing hierarchy. • Item library evidence from KG trials is limited —  all five PI trials used full QLQ-C30/MY20 instruments rather than calibrated short forms . Consider whether abbreviated assessment approach is appropriate given weekly dosing schedule (Table 2, Total items column). •  Real-world MM data shows bone pain affects 47.2% of patient responses with mean EORTC QLQ-C30 pain score of 1.80 , confirming bone pain as clinically relevant endpoint for this population. However, this reinforces the need for dedicated bone pain measurement beyond generic QLQ-C30 pain subscale. •  EQ-5D-5L requires country-specific value sets and is not universally mappable to 3L  (Table 5, EQ-5D-5L row) — critical for multi-regional trial with NICE/ICER submissions requiring precise utility calculations per jurisdiction.

## Comparator Analysis

**carfilzomib** — Proteasome inhibitor — EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20, EQ-5D-5L, CSQ-8, FACT/GOG-NTX — Mixed outcomes across three trials (IKEMA: not reported, A.R.R.O.W.: significant p<0.01, ENDEAVOR: significant p<0.001) — supports EORTC instruments' sensitivity but suggests effect size varies by combination regimen and patient population.

**ixazomib** — Proteasome inhibitor — EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20 — Significant improvements p<0.05 in TOURMALINE-MM3 but null results in TOURMALINE-MM4 — indicates that oral PI formulation may have different tolerability profile affecting PRO outcomes, relevant for differentiating IV step-up dosing advantages.

No same-mechanism next-generation PI comparator data identified in KG trials.  Expert should review recent FDA and EMA medical reviews for novel PI submissions to assess PRO precedent for regulatory acceptance .

Based on comparator evidence,  EORTC QLQ-C30/MY20 combination has demonstrated change detection in 3/5 PI trials  with significant results correlating with approved drug combinations, suggesting adequate sensitivity for this mechanism class.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In Candidate List? | Action Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L with England value set | Yes | Confirm England value set implementation and country-specific scoring algorithm |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L for QALY calculation | Yes | Confirm US population value set availability and cost-effectiveness modelling requirements |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to supplement QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale with a dedicated bone pain instrument (e.g., BPI-SF) for stronger regulatory support of bone pain claims. 2. Assessment schedule frequency balancing weekly dosing cycle alignment with patient burden — current candidate battery totals 65+ items requiring 25-30 minutes. 3. PRO-CTCAE inclusion for symptomatic adverse event assessment versus relying on QLQ-MY20 Side Effects subscale for treatment tolerability claims. 4. Hierarchical testing position for PRO endpoints — whether to position QLQ-C30 global health status as key secondary endpoint following PFS/OS or maintain all PRO endpoints as exploratory. 5. BFI fatigue assessment versus QLQ-C30 fatigue subscale trade-off — dedicated instrument provides stronger regulatory precedent but increases patient burden in already lengthy battery.
